programme.desc: Strongman Champions League 2025 opens in Joensuu, Finland in freezing -5°C conditions. Athletes battle frame carry as first event on ice and snow. Brian Kichton sets early pace, but Kevin Hazeleger ultimately wins with 27.57s. Competitors from USA, Finland, Turkey and others struggle with cold and debut performances, setting the tone for a global season. Cold conditions define the opening stage.

programme.title: Strongman Champions League 2025

Events include truck pull, log lift, bag toss medley, loading race and Atlas Stones. Home favourite Aivars Smaukstelis returns in emotional final Latvian appearance aiming for his third SCL crown. The competition begins with a truck pull opener setting early times.

programme.title: Strongman Champions League 2025
programme.desc: Strongman Champions League 2025 heads to Zrenjanin, Serbia for Stage 3, where elite athletes compete in a packed city-centre showdown. With four debutants joining established names like Evans Nana and Aivars Smaukstelis, competitors face brutal tests including a 16,000kg truck pull as the season builds momentum.

programme.title: Strongman Champions League 2025
programme.desc: Strongman Champions League 2025 kicks off in Crema, Italy, for Stage 4 of the season, bringing a world-class lineup to Lombardy. Athletes face brutal tests including car deadlift, log lift medley, Hercules hold, and Atlas stones, as reigning champion Rayno Nel returns fresh from major victory to defend his crown.

programme.title: Strongman Champions League 2025
programme.desc: Strongman Champions League returns to Doetinchem, Netherlands, for a high-stakes summer showdown. A world-class lineup, including Rayno Nel, Brian Kichton, and Evans Nana, battles in extreme 35°C heat across six brutal events such as truck pull, Viking press, and Atlas stones, as the fight for SCL glory intensifies.

programme.title: Strongman Champions League 2025
programme.desc: Strongman Champions League returns to Doetinchem, Holland, for Stage 5 as athletes resume Day 2 of competition in a tight battle for the SCL title. Other highlights include the Front Hold with a whiskey barrel, a keg toss into water, and a gruelling 130,000 kg boat pull - capped off by an electrifying Guinness World Record attempt.

programme.title: Bing

Bing is sad when he is told, after having had his vaccination, that there are none of his favourite stickers left at Dr Molly’s surgery. He soon cheers up though when he is given a very special certificate instead.

What could it be and where will they find it?

programme.title: Cleasan Ataidh & Tilidh/The Adventures of Abney & Teal
programme.desc: Tha cuid dhe na rudan as fheàrr le Àtaidh agus Tilidh a dhìth. A bheil cuideigin air an goid? ’S e rùn-dìomhair a th’ ann! Some of Abney and Teal’s favourite objects are missing. Has there been a robbery? It’s a mystery!

programme.title: ’S E Iasg a Th’Annam (I’m a Fish)
programme.desc: Tha an t-Iasg Ceann-chaorach gu math lìogach - tha fiaclan orra a dh’itheas cha mhòr rud sam bith agus tha iad math air biathadh nan iasgair a ghoid, gun duine greim fhaighinn orra. The Sheepshead Fish is very sneaky - they can eat pretty much anything as they have very sharp teeth and can steal the bait off fishing hooks, without getting caught.

programme.title: Peataichean/Pets
programme.desc: Tha Eilidh NicCarmaig a’ coinneachadh ri clann agus a’ faighinn a-mach mu mar a tha iad a’ coimhead às dèidh agus a’ cluich cuide rim peataichean aig an taigh. Anns a’ phrògram seo tha Eilidh a’ cèilidh air Angus agus na ceithir cait spòrsail aige. Gheibh sinn a-mach barrachd mu bhith a’ coimhead às dèidh cait agus mu na rudan snog is spòrsail a bhios Angus, Parlsey, Jasper, Roxy agus Dylan a’ dèanamh còmhla. Gheibh sinn cuideachd comhairle agus fiosrachadh bho Eilidh fhèin mu bhith a’ làimhseachadh, ag oideachadh agus a’ coimhead às dèidh peataichean. Eilidh Cormack meets young children who are pet owners. Together they show, tell and share how they care for, play and interact with their pets at home. In this episode, Eilidh visits Angus and his four handsome and fun-loving cats. We find out how to look after cats and about all the lovely stuff Angus, Jasper, Parsley, Roxy and Dylan get up to together. Eilidh also shares fun and interesting facts along with advice on looking after pets at home - including how best to handle, train and feed them.

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Tha Sona air a bhith trang a’ fàsgadh dhearcan ach tha e air cus den t-sùgh òl – tha sin ga fhàgail nas beòthail’ ‘s nas toilicht’ na bha e o chionn fhada. Abair gu bheil deagh ghumbladh a’ gabhail àit’! Sona has been busy pulping berries but he’s drunk too much of the juice - this has made him livelier and happier than he’s been for quite a while. There’s a lot of Gumbling taking place!

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Tha an dithis mhealltair – Merri is Seonaidh – ri miastadh. Nuair a tha ’ad a' toirt seachad gheallaidhean nach meall ’ad na Gumbalan, tha ’ad a' tionndadh gus feuchainn ris a’ char a thoirt às na Bògaisean. Saoil ciamar a thèid dhaibh? The two tricksters, Merri and Seonaidh, are up to no good. When they promise not to trick the Gumbals, they turn to playing mischief on the Bògaisean. How will they get on?

programme.title: Seonaidh | Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: Tha Bitzer air fois fhaighinn agus Seonaidh bochd fo gheasaibh aig Mowermouth an Gobhair. Ge-tà leis an treud air fad fo smachd Mowermouth, tha Bitzer a' tuigse gu bheil feum aige air a dheagh charaid. Bitzer gets his wish for some peace and quiet when Shaun becomes hypnotised by Mowermouth the goat and finally stops bothering him. But with the whole flock under the influence of Mowermouth's powerful gaze, Bitzer soon realises just how much he needs his old buddy.

programme.title: Hilda
programme.desc: Tha Hilda a’ tionndadh gu leabhar dìomhair airson ionnsachadh mar a chuidicheas i beathannan Dhaibhidh agus a màthair – ach, mo chreach, abair gu ‘eil a coibhneis cosgail is croiseil dhaibh uile. Hilda turns to a mysterious book to learn how she can better the lives of Daibhidh and her mother, but being kind proves to be costly and problematic for all.

programme.title: Fillte
programme.desc: Fillte travels throughout Scotland, visiting the country’s finest woven craft producers. Tha Fillte a siuhbail fad Alba a lorg an obair-laimhne is fhearr, sa luchd-ciùird fighe a chruthaich e.

programme.desc: A mockumentary shadowing a company that services short term lets. Angela and Katie aim to clean-up and give the competition a bleaching. Blockages need to be dealt with, not just unclogging hot tub filters. A new staff member has a few skeletons in his cupboard but ex-con Daniel hopes he has a squeaky-clean future. Meanwhile, Betty meets Daniel’s pregnant partner Dido and checks in on her beloved pet pooch Buster. Soon the police are knocking on the company’s portacabin door. Written by and starring Hannah McKirdy and Lana Pheutan.

programme.desc: Shetland’s expansive coastline is home to endless towering cliffs, but its remoteness from the mainland means they see few ascents. With a friend in tow, Coinneach Rankin travels to Shetland in search of new routes and spectacular climbing challenges. Tha oirthir fhada Shealtainn loma làn chreagan tomadach agus seallaidhean nach creidear, ach air sgàth cho cèin ’s a tha i bho thir-mòr, chan fhaigh cus an cothrom sreap ann. programme.desc: Tha rèis dhan bhàrr dol bhith ann – a’ chiad oileanach a chuireas flaga air Beinn Rocaid a' buinnig na duais. Ach bheil cuideigin na chealgaire? A race to the summit is going to take place - the first student to plant a flag on Mount Rocket will win the trophy. But is somebody a cheat?

programme.desc: Tha Bitzer air crìoch a chuir air an obair-taighe gu lèir agus a-nis chan eil càil aige ri dhèanamh. The e air a dhòigh nuair a mhothachas e gu bheil an t-sabhal feumach air sgioblachadh - gus an tig e tairsinn air dealbh nach gabh a chrochadh gu dìreach! Bitzer has completed all his chores and is at a bit of a loss. He's delighted when he discovers the flock's barn needs a good tidy-up, until he comes across a wonky picture that just won't hang straight.

Abigail’s favourite snack lunch is crispy sage potatoes. It's as nice to look at as to eat and her version is easy to make - you must try it! In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Fonn mo Bheatha
programme.desc: Ceòl agus còmhradh le Cathy Ann Nic a Phi còmhla ri Cairistiona Cheannadach. Music and chat programme presented by Cathy Ann MacPhee with guest Kristine Kennedy.

programme.desc: Murdo Macdonald explores the Japanese Garden at Cowden. Murchadh Dòmhnallach a’cur eòlas air Gàrradh Siapanach Cowden faisg air Dollar.

programme.title: Mas Fhior
programme.desc: Farpais-cheist do-chreidsinneach... Mas Fhìor! Le ochdnar Mas Fhìoraich a’ cluich bhon dachaighean fhèin, ’s iad an fheadhainn a chuireas na ceistean agus na freagairtean. An urrainn do Isla is Hamish agus Jamie is Liam a tha a’ cluich bhon stiùideo a’ chùis a dhèanamh orra airson an duais mhòr a bhuannachadh? A quiz show that is pretty unbelievable! Eight Pretenders play from the comfort of their own homes and hold all the questions and answers to this quiz. Can Isla and Hamish, or Jamie and Liam in the studio beat the Pretenders for a chance to win a cash prize? In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Steelmen
programme.desc: Ann an 1991, bha baile Thobar na Màthar a’ greimeachadh ris a’ bhuaidh shòisealta, eaconamach agus chultarail a bheireadh dùnadh ionad stàilinn Ravenscraig air an sgìre, ach airson a’ chiad uair ann an 39 bliadhna thog sgioba ball-coise a’ bhaile, na ‘Steelmen' mar a theirear riutha, Cupa na h-Alba, a’ toirt boillsgeadh dòchais a thogadh an dorchadas. In 1991, as the town of Motherwell faced the crippling social, economic and cultural impact of the closure of the Ravenscraig steelworks, its football club, locally known as the Steelmen, lifted the prestigious Scottish Cup for the first time in 39 years. The victory was a glimmer of light in the ensuing darkness.

programme.title: Ciad-fàthan nan Creutairean/Wild Senses

programme.title: SPFL
programme.desc: Ball-coise bho Lìog a h-Aon le Hamilton Academical a’ cur fàilte air Ross County, beò air BBC ALBA. An geama beò ri fhaicinn le preasantair Alasdair MacIllinnein agus aithris bho Ailig O’Henley. Join BBC Alba for live League 1 football action as Hamilton Academical host Ross County. Full coverage with presenter Alasdair MacLennan and commentary from Alex O’Henley.

programme.title: Rurachd (Foraging)
programme.desc: Mary Ann Kennedy and Lucy Cooke: a foraged feast with musical friends in Galloway. Màiri Anna NicUalraig agus Liusaidh Cooke le stòras nàdair. Ròic na Rùrachd le càirdean ciùil an Gall Ghàidhealaibh.

programme.title: Faodail
programme.desc: Tha Tasglann Fhilm Faodail a’ tarraing aire gu filmichean dhùthchasach Innse Gall bho na 1930an gu na 80an, a bha caillte ach a-nis glèidhte don ghinealach ri teachd. Tha bhana Cinema Sgìre Leantainneach a’ siubhal nan eilean, a’ taisbeanadh fhilmichean sna sgìrean ionadail, le cothrom am faicinn air-loidhne air feadh an t-saoghail. Cuirear aithris bheairteach ùr riutha, a’ buntainn ris a’ Ghàidhealtachd, airson luchd-amhairc an là an-diugh. The Faodail Film Archive celebrates lost indigenous film collections from the 1930s-1980s in the Outer Hebrides, preserving the archive for future generations. The Cinema Sgìre Continuing mobile cinema van travels the islands, showcasing footage to local communities, making them accessible globally online and adding rich new narratives relevant to the Gàidhealtachd for contemporary audiences. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Dàna | Scotland's Wild Side
programme.desc: Shetland’s expansive coastline is home to endless towering cliffs, but its remoteness from the mainland means they see few ascents. With a friend in tow, Coinneach Rankin travels to Shetland in search of new routes and spectacular climbing challenges. Tha oirthir fhada Shealtainn loma làn chreagan tomadach agus seallaidhean nach creidear, ach air sgàth cho cèin ’s a tha i bho thir-mòr, chan fhaigh cus an cothrom sreap ann. Le seann charaid na chuideachd, siubhailidh Coinneach MacFhraing a Shealtainn air tòir slighean ùra is dùbhlain bharraichte. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Rathad Ramsay
programme.desc: Ramsay meets Kim Carnie on the island of Kerrera, where they walk along picturesque bays with panoramic views of Oban Bay and the Slate Islands. Kim discusses the importance of Gaelic in her life and how that has shaped her career as a singer. She opens up about love and identity, and how that has evolved over the years, whilst enjoying the surrounding nature and fresh autumn air. San treas sreath de Rathad Ramsay bidh Ramsay MacMahon a’ coinneachadh ri sàr Ghàidheil bho air feadh Alba ‘s iad a’ co-roinn sgeulachdan, cuir luach air nàdar agus a’ cnuasachadh ma beatha. Tha Ramsay a’ coinneachadh ri Kim Carnie air eilean Chearrara far a bheil iad air an cuartachadh le bàghean àlainn agus seallaidhean air leth den Òban agus na h-Eileanan Sglèata. Innsidh Kim cho cudromach ‘s a tha Gàidhlig na beatha ‘s a bhuaidh a tha seo air a thoirt air a beatha agus air a dreuchd na seinneadair. Gu follaiseach dèidheil air àm an fhoghair agus an àrainneachd ghlan mun cuairt, tha i fuasgladh suas ma beachdan air gaol, fèin-aithne agus mar a tha sin air obrachadh a-mach na beatha fhèin. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Seirm
programme.desc: Prògram de cheòl traidiseanta agus freumhach air a lìbhrigeadh le Màiri Anna NicUalraig. A’ taisbeanaidh chlàraidhean is chòmhraidhean a chaidh a dhèanamh aig àm Celtic Connections 2024, chìte cuid den luchd-ciùil a b’ fheàrr a bha aig an fhèis, leithid Talisk, Julie Fowlis/Éamon Doorley/Zoë Conway/John Mc Intyre, Glen Hansard & Breanndán Ó Beaglaoich, Buffalo Nichols agus Pine Tree Flyers. Traditional and roots music show presented by Mary Ann Kennedy. Filmed during Celtic Connections 2024, Seirm showcases bespoke recordings and conversations with some of the best artists appearing at the festival. This episode features performances from Talisk; Julie Fowlis, Éamon Doorley, Zoë Conway, John McIntyre; Glen Hansard & Breanndán Ó Beaglaoich, Buffalo Nichols and Pine Tree Flyers. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Ro Thrath don t-Saoghal/Born too Soon
programme.desc: Obair sgioba an Aonad Dlùth-chùram Leanabain ’s iad a’ coimhead an dèidh naoidheanan so-leònta. The work of the NICU team and their care for vulnerable babies.

programme.title: Fraochy Bay
programme.desc: Thàinig an ola gu Fraochy Bay ach de a' bhuaidh a tha e air a thoirt air a' bhaile agus na daoine? Agus de cho fada sa sheasas e, agus de ni muinntir a' bhaile leis an dìleab? Fraochy Bay has experienced an oil boom, but just as quickly as it arrived it dries up, causing a swift departure of the oil industry. How will the townsfolk deal with the leftovers?

programme.title: Abigail
programme.desc: An greimean lòin as fheàrr le Abigail, 's e Buntàta Cruasbach Sàiste. 'Ad cho blast' 's a tha 'ad rin ithe. Tha 'n seòrs' aice-se soirbh a dhèanamh; feumaidh tu fheuchainn. Abigail’s favourite snack lunch is crispy sage potatoes. It's as nice to look at as to eat and her version is easy to make - you must try it! In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Steelmen
programme.desc: Ann an 1991, bha baile Thobar na Màthar a’ greimeachadh ris a’ bhuaidh shòisealta, eaconamach agus chultarail a bheireadh dùnadh ionad stàilinn Ravenscraig air an sgìre, ach airson a’ chiad uair ann an 39 bliadhna thog sgioba ball-coise a’ bhaile, na ‘Steelmen' mar a theirear riutha, Cupa na h-Alba, a’ toirt boillsgeadh dòchais a thogadh an dorchadas. In 1991, as the town of Motherwell faced the crippling social, economic and cultural impact of the closure of the Ravenscraig steelworks, its football club, locally known as the Steelmen, lifted the prestigious Scottish Cup for the first time in 39 years. The victory was a glimmer of light in the ensuing darkness.

programme.title: Belladrum
programme.desc: Fiona NicChoinnich agus Niall Iain Dòmhnallach a’ cur fàilte air luchd-amhairc chun a’ chuid às fheàrr de Fhèis Belladrum 2022. Anns a' phrògram seo, cothrom am prìomh thaisbeanadh air Àrd-ùrlar a Ghàrraidh bho oidhche Dhiardaoin na Fèise fhaicinn. Bha an t-àite loma-làn airson an taisbeanadh aig an t-seinneadair chliùiteach Emile Sandé, a tha air soirbheachadh mu mòr mar sgrìobhaiche òran agus air na milleanan de chlàran album a reic air feadh an t-saoghail. Fiona MacKenzie and Niall Iain MacDonald host highlights from the Belladrum festival, 2022. This programme features the headlining act from the Garden Stage on Thursday night at the festival. Performing in front of a packed audience was acclaimed singer Emeli Sandé, one of Britain’s most successful songwriters, having sold millions of albums worldwide.

programme.title: Skipinnish Aig A' Chaisteal
programme.desc: Skipinnish le Last of the Hunters ann an cuideachd na mìltean de luchd-leantainn aig cuirm-chiùil a’ comharrachadh 25 bliadhna de Skipinnish, bho Chaisteal Dhùn Èideann. Skipinnish perform Last of the Hunters in front of thousands of fans at a concert celebrating 25 years of the band, from Edinburgh Castle.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Losgannan | Froglets
programme.desc: Le cuideachadh bho Burtaidh, tha Sif a’ toirt Pipp agus Bran air dàn-chuairt fèill spòrs. Ziff leads Pipp and Button on a fairground adventure with help from faithful Bertie.

programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Tha Bèibidh Dràgon Brot’ mì-thoilichte oir chan fhaod e cluich leis an spàin bhrot’ oir tha ro mhòr dha. Gu fortanach, tha Beag a’ moladh gum faod e taic a thoirt dhaibh-san le bhith toirt am brot air ais dhan uamh – is abair g’eil e taiceil! Baby Soup Dragon is unhappy - he isn’t allowed to play with the soup spoon as it’s too big for him. Fortunately, Small suggests that he can help to deliver the soup instead - and he is hugely helpful!

programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Tha bogsa dìomhaireachd air laighe air a’ phlanaid, le rudan annasach na bhroinn - clobhdan a tha nan tuill cuideachd. Tha e comasach dha na Clangairean siubhal tro na tuill seo - agus abair gu bheil iad trang a’ siubhal! A mysterious box has landed on the planet, with curious things inside it - cloths which are also holes. The Clangers can travel through these holes, and they do it a lot!

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha a’ ghrian a’ deàrrsadh ‘s tha Ooona'son dhol a dh’iasgach. Tha May ag aontachadh cluich cuide ri Baba ach tha Baba a’ diùltadh faiche nan gràineag fhàgail gus an dùisg Spiky bho chadal-geamhraidh! It’s a beautiful day and Oona wants to practise fishing. May offers to play with Baba, who refuses to leave the hedghog burrow as he wants to wait until Spiky wakes from his hibernation!

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha Oona daonnan ann an cabhag ach tha Papa airson sealltainn dhi gum bi buthaidean a' gabhail cùisean air an socair. Saoil an tig aice air ionnsachadh rudan a dhèanamh ann an ‘Dòigh na Buthaide? Oona is forever in a hurry to learn and get things done, but Papa wants to show her that puffins tend to approach things in a slow and steady fashion. Will Oona master the ‘Way of the Puffin?’

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Nuair a tha Sula a’ tadhal air Bing ‘s i air a h-aodann a pheantadh mar dhealan-dè, tha i airson aodann Bing a’ pheantadh cuideachd. Chaneil am peantadh a' dol ro mhath ach tha e sealbhach gu bheil Flop ri làimh airson gnothaichean a rèiteachadh. When Sula visits Bing with her face painted like a butterfly, she also wants to face paint Bing. But the painting doesn’t go well for them. Fortunately, Flop is on hand to sort it all out.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Tha Bing brònach nuair a thèid innse dha, an-dèidh dha a’ bhanachdach fhaighinn, nach eil gin de na steigearan sònraichte as fheàrr leis air fhàgail. Tha cùisean ag atharrachadh ge-tà nuair a tha e a’ faighinn teisteanas grinn, sònraichte. Bing is sad when he is told, after having had his vaccination, that there are none of his favourite stickers left at Dr Molly’s surgery. He soon cheers up though when he is given a very special certificate instead.

programme.title: Peicein/Petit
programme.desc: Tha tòrr spòrs aig Peicein is a charaidean a’ cur an ìre gur e ròbotan a th’ annta, gus am brùth cuideigin aca putan is tha an aileag a’ tòiseachadh air Peicein. Carson nach stad an aileag aige? Bheil smachd aig cuideigin air à àiteigin eile? Chan urrainn do Ghriogair sguir a shreothartaich, Lòra a mhèaranaich neo Raghnall a chasadaich. Saoil a bheil iad uile a’ tionndadh nan ròbotan dhà-rìribh? Petit and his friends are having a lot of fun pretending to be robots, until one of them presses a button and Petit gets the hiccups. Why can't he stop hiccupping? Is someone else controlling him from somewhere? Greg can't stop sneezing, Laura yawns and Roman coughs. Could it be that everyone is turning into real life robots?

programme.title: Hilda
programme.desc: Tha Hilda a’ tionndadh gu leabhar dìomhair airson ionnsachadh mar a chuidicheas i beathannan Dhaibhidh agus a màthair – ach, mo chreach, abair gu ‘eil a coibhneis cosgail is croiseil dhaibh uile. Hilda turns to a mysterious book to learn how she can better the lives of Daibhidh and her mother, but being kind proves to be costly and problematic for all.

programme.title: Flix
programme.desc: Nuair tha Greta an cù a’ cèilidh air an sgoil, tha Flix airson a bhith taiceil dhi. Gu mì-fhortanach tha iad glè mhì-mhodhail nuair a tha ‘ad còmhla. Tha seo ag adhbharachadh trioblaid coin-cait ach the feum air fuasgladh cait-coin. When Greta the dog visits the school, Flix wants to be helpful to her. Unfortunately, they’re very badly behaved when together. This causes a dog-cat problem so what’s needed is a cat-dog solution!

programme.title: Geamaichean Gorach
programme.desc: Tha cùisean a-dol ceàrr leis na Farpaisich ach tha a’ Chrùbag faisg air làimh le cobhair, tòrr ruitheam agus an 'cha cha cha'! Things go awry with the competitors, but Crùbag is near to hand, with lots of rhythm and the 'cha cha cha'!

programme.title: A-null ’s a-nall
programme.desc: Tha Isra cho toilichte nuair a tha i a’ faighinn an cothrom càmpadh mar a sìnnsearan - na Bedouin - còmhla ri a caraid, Laoise. Isra is delighted when she gets the chance to go camping like her ancestors, the Bedouin, with her friend, Laoise.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Local, national and international news from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Seachd Là
programme.desc: Local, national and international news from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Alleluia!
programme.desc: Ann am prògram às an tasglann bho 2009, Salm 31 air a sheinn le Ceathrar-cheòil Còisir Ghàidhlig Ìleach Ghlaschu, Laoidh Chalum Chille le Còisir Ghàidhlig Bhaile Ghobhainn agus bidh Torcuil MacLeòid ag innse mun phàirt a th' aig creideamh na bheatha fhèin. Air aithris le Iain MacFhionghain. In an archival edition from 2009, Psalm 31 sung by the Glasgow Islay Gaelic Choir Quartet, the hymn Laoidh Chalum Chille by Govan Gaelic Choir, and Torquil MacLeod tells his personal faith story. Presented by Iain MacKinnon. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Cidsin Granaidh Chalanais
programme.desc: Gregor makes his grannie’s gingerbread and classic Scottish tablet, and adds his own flair to her fishcake recipe.

programme.title: Rùm Gu Rùm, Le Erica
programme.desc: Actress turned interior designer, Erica Macpherson, takes us on a design adventure throughout the Highlands and Islands. With the help of local craft workers she finds new ideas for designing old spaces. Tha an cleasaiche, a tha a-nis na dealbhaiche cruthachail thaighean, Erica Nic a’ Phersain, a’ gabhail sgrìob tron Ghàidhealtachd ‘s na h-Eileanan. Le taic bho luchd-ciùird, tha i a’ lorg dhòighean ùra air seann rumanan a thoirt beò. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Surfing: Marcachd an Tuinn/Riding the Wave
programme.desc: Tha Ceitlin Lilidh a’ toirt thugainn sreath de dhà phàirt air eachdraidh surfadh air feadh an t-saoghail. Ceitlin Lilidh's series on the world history of surfing.

programme.desc: We explore the surprising ways animals use touch to sense their world, find food and stay out of danger.

programme.title: Fred Dibnah's Magnificent Monuments
programme.desc: Steeplejack Fred Dibnah visits Hampton Court Palace and Cragside, one of the first homes to have electric lighting. He also examines restoration work on a 15th-century manor house.

programme.title: War Walks
programme.desc: Wellington's victory against Napoleon in 1815 ended the most powerful European empire since the Romans. Professor Holmes visits the farms and fields where history hung in the balance.

programme.title: The Planets
programme.desc: Professor Brian Cox reveals the history of Saturn, which began life as a strange world of rock and ice. In time, it transformed into a gas giant, ring-less and similar looking to its rival, Jupiter.

programme.title: A Wild Year
programme.desc: A look at Pembrokeshire’s wild and rugged coast, where life is defined by the rhythm of the seasons and the power of the sea.

programme.title: War Walks
programme.desc: The British troops who marched against the Germans in August 1914 believed the war would be over by Christmas. But at Mons they learned that the old world of swords and bugles would be swept away by the machine gun and the shell. Richard Holmes follows in their footsteps as they retreated south from Mons.

programme.title: The Battle of the River Plate
programme.desc: Second World War naval adventure based on the true story of the pursuit of the seemingly unstoppable German battleship Graf Spee. Allied forces chase the vessel all the way to South America, but after several failed attempts to sink the enemy ship, the Allies find themselves hatching a desperate and audacious plan.

programme.title: Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy
programme.desc: Film adaptation of John Le Carre's Cold War novel about a retired MI6 agent who must track down a Soviet mole within the British intelligence service's ranks.

programme.title: Mark Kermode's Secrets of Cinema
programme.desc: Mark Kermode explores one of the most distinctive and popular genres of all. The spy movie plays on our paranoia and feeds our fears as well as fulfilling our fantasies of secret missions and special skills. It has also given us perhaps the most famous hero in all of cinema – James Bond. Spy movies capture a world not of black and white but shades of grey. But if the morality is often ambiguous, the genre is full of tried and tested conventions. Mark opens up the cinematic agent’s essential toolkit, from the spy boss to the mysterious McGuffin, surveillance techniques to a striking set of opening titles, and he traces the development of the genre from its earliest days. Whether you’re a blockbuster superspy or a compromised cold warrior, Mark reveals all you need to survive in the murky yet thrilling world of big screen espionage.

programme.title: In Conversation
programme.desc: Actor Cillian Murphy, who played the lead role in Ken Loach's Palme d'Or-winning film The Wind That Shakes the Barley, talks to the director at the BFI Southbank about a prolific career dedicated to documenting social and political injustice, the importance of artistic collaboration, the often-overlooked humour in Loach's films, and the impact working with Loach had on his own approach to acting.

programme.title: Timeshift
programme.desc: What happens when a literary novelist tries to write popular romantic fiction? To mark 100 years of romance publishers Mills and Boon, literary novelist Stella Duffy takes on the challenge of writing for them. Romantic fiction is a global phenomenon, and Mills and Boon are among the biggest names in the business. The company welcomes submissions from new authors, but as Duffy soon finds out, writing a Mills and Boon is harder than it looks. Help is at hand from the publishers themselves, a prolific Mills and Boon author and some avid romance fans, as Duffy's quest to create the perfect romantic novel takes her from London to Italy on a journey that is both an insight into the art of romantic fiction and the joy and frustration of writing itself.

programme.title: Girls in Bands at the BBC
programme.desc: Compilation celebrating some guitar band performances at the BBC that feature some of the best female musicians in rock. Beginning with the oft-forgotten American group Fanny performing You're the One, it's a journey along rock's spectrum from the 1970s to now. The selection includes the powerful vocals of Elkie Brooks on Vinegar Joe's Proud to Be a Honky Woman, the mesmerising poetry of Patti Smith's Horses and the upbeat energy of The Go-Go's on We Got the Beat. Mighty basslines come courtesy of Tina Weymouth on Psycho Killer and Kim Gordon on Sugar Kane, whilst we trace the line of indie rock from the Au Pairs through Lush, Elastica and Garbage to current band Savages.

programme.title: Rock Goes to College
programme.desc: Pete Drummond introduces Siouxsie and the Banshees in concert at Warwick University.

programme.title: Fanny: The Right to Rock
programme.desc: The untold story of one of the earliest all-female rock groups, who, almost 50 years after disbanding, have a new record deal and a chance to right the wrongs of history.

programme.title: Wild
programme.desc: Documentary presenting an intimate portrait of one of Britain's most charming wild animals, following a family of water voles living on a canal in Derbyshire though a typical year. The picturesque Cromford canal used to serve the region's cotton mills. Now, having been deserted, it serves as a perfect water vole paradise. For these hyperactive little mammals, a year is nearly a lifetime. They spend their lives in a frenzy of activity - swimming, feeding and breeding - the latter of most necessity, since water voles are becoming a rarity.

programme.title: Full Circle with Michael Palin
programme.desc: Michael Palin circles the Pacific Rim through 18 countries. After a journey on a rusty ferry through the dangerous Sulu Sea, he arrives in Borneo at monsoon time. From the rainforest, he heads off to the long houses of the Iban tribesmen and the secret heart of Borneo. Across the equator in Java, the most densely populated island in the world, he visits the largest monument in the southern hemisphere.

programme.title: Miss Marple
programme.desc: In the late 1940s, Gerry Burton, accompanied by his sister Joanna, goes to the little village of Lymston to convalesce after an accident. The village seems to welcome them with open arms. But there are dark mysterious undercurrents at work and it's not long before Miss Marple comes to visit.

programme.title: Around the World in 80 Treasures
programme.desc: Dan is captivated by the sword of a Samurai warrior and the artistry employed to make this beautiful instrument of death. By contrast, he finds solace and tranquillity in a Japanese temple and meditation garden.

programme.title: Ran
programme.desc: Akira Kurosawa's epic masterpiece is a reworking of Shakespeare's King Lear set in medieval Japan. After a lifetime of battles, 70-year-old Lord Hidetora announces that he is passing his authority to his eldest son Taro. The youngest son Saburo protests and is banished from the kingdom. But instead of fulfilling their father's wishes, Taro and middle brother Jiro are disloyal to the former lord and attack his castle. Hidetora survives but following his sons' betrayal is now losing his mind. When Jiro has his brother murdered, the banished Saburo and his allies return to fight a battle against the remaining brother. In Japanese with English subtitles.

programme.title: Arena
programme.desc: Sam Shepard narrates a documentary profile of celebrated Japanese film-maker Akira Kurosawa, responsible for the films Seven Samurai, Ikiru and Rashomon.

programme.title: To the Manor Born

programme.title: The Medici: Makers of Modern Art
programme.desc: Documentary in which Andrew Graham-Dixon reveals how the Medici family transformed Florence through sculpture, painting and architecture, and created a world where masterpieces fetch millions today. Without the money and patronage of the Medici we might never have heard of artists such as Donatello, Michelangelo or Botticelli. Graham-Dixon examines how a family of shadowy, corrupt businessmen, driven by greed and ambition, became the financial engine behind the Italian Renaissance.

programme.desc: Scottish Opera's sparkling staging of Gilbert and Sullivan's witty satire. Audiences are transported to Venice for a joyful production packed with some of the pair's most-loved songs.

Adrienne Murray is in Iceland exploring innovations in food production. Megha Mohan meets Meredith Whittaker, president of the Signal Foundation and one of the most influential women in AI. And Zoe Kleinman tries out the latest smart glasses.

programme.title: AI Decoded
programme.desc: Would you let AI walk around your home? We explore the growing race to put humanoid robots into our homes and workplaces. We examine Meta's reported robot project, the rise of Chinese robot manufacturers, the privacy risks of machines that can see, hear and map our lives and whether robots are becoming Big Tech's next multi-trillion-dollar bet. Meta has reportedly built a humanoid robot called Max and, if Mark Zuckerberg gets his way, this could be the next frontier for artificial intelligence. After years of AI living on our screens, Silicon Valley is now racing to give AI a body, one that can see, hear, move through the world and interact with people in real life. Could a humanoid robot really become as common as a smartphone? Would you trust one to help around the house, care for an elderly relative, or perform tasks at work? And as companies spend hundreds of billions of dollars on AI, are robots the breakthrough the industry has been waiting for, or another expensive gamble destined to disappoint?

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Today’s show comes from a bustling antiques fair in Detling in Kent, where two teams browse jam-packed stalls with the aim of buying three items in an hour to take to auction. The red team, friends Bill and Al, known as Del Boy and Rodney to their friends, are led around by expert Catherine Southon, while the blues, performing arts teachers Jo and Simisola, are treated to the dry wit of expert Mark Stacey. Both teams browse a variety of items, but whereas the blues finish with enough time to grab a cuppa, the reds take it right to the wire. With the seconds counting down, Bill, Al and Catherine desperately try to find their third item. Will they do a deal in time? Presenter Eric Knowles visits the Kent Museum of the Moving Image to learn about peep boxes and magic lanterns, two early forms of visual entertainment that delighted audiences as far back as the 17th century. Over in Portsmouth, auctioneer Daniel Tricker is doing the business on the rostrum.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Ollie, Gus, Benjy and Joe – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Grand Tours of Scotland's Rivers
programme.desc: This surprising grand tour follows the river Ythan in rural Aberdeenshire, which flows through a landscape of wheat fields and haunted castles and on to a coast rich in wildlife. On the way, Paul Murton learns how to make a haystack, speak the local 'Doric' and has a ghostly encounter with a woman in Fyvie Castle. He visits Gight Castle, the ruined home of poet Lord Byron’s family. Journey’s end is at the mouth of the river, where sand dunes have created Scotland’s version of the Sahara.

programme.title: My Husband the MMA Fighter
programme.desc: Documentary. The story of Stevie ‘Braveheart’ Ray’s million-dollar cage fight, told through the eyes of his wife, Natalie.

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: Dougie is in Castlemilk housing estate on the southern edge of Glasgow, where he explores a local nature reserve that has transformed from perceived no-go zone to a thriving, green place. Arlene steps back in time in Aberdeenshire as she visits a rare shoemaker's workshop that shut up shop over 80 years ago. She meets the locals carefully conserving the shop’s contents. Anne is in the Black Isle, finding out about a charity funded by Children in Need that is providing bereavement support across the Highlands. And Dougie watches on as one couple’s herd of Aberdeen Angus cattle leaves the farm for good to go under the hammer at a dispersal sale.

And the traffic cops lift a street vigilante planting greenery in potholes.

programme.title: The Chief

programme.desc: Sarah the Lumberjill is the fourth generation of her family to 'take up the saw', working across the forests of the Central Highlands of Scotland, where her family have worked for 150 years. After some of the worst storms to hit Scotland in a lifetime, Sarah, her dad Ralph and brother Ralphy are busier than ever - though with Ralph's health in decline, Sarah has a lot to learn before taking over one day.

programme.title: Highland Cops
programme.desc: A knife attack in Inverness leads police to a volatile suspect and a house packed with blades, from Samurai swords to machetes and zombie knives. Released on bail while police await DNA results, he is soon wanted over another violent attack. On the Isle of Skye, rescuers race to find a climber who has been missing for three days in the mountains. And near Fort William, an American tourist has an unusual concern after a crash.

programme.title: Mythland
programme.desc: Deep in the Highlands, Loch Morar is home to a mysterious legend: Morag, a creature said to lurk beneath its dark, cold waters. Comedian and ecologist Zara Gladman teams up with parapsychologist Evelyn Hollow to investigate the sightings and meet locals whose accounts have kept the story alive for generations. A loch superintendent recalls a strange wake racing across the water, an angler describes three huge humps rising behind his boat, and a lifelong monster hunter reveals how easily shadows can fool even experts. As Zara gathers environmental DNA from the loch, could science finally offer an explanation? The results point to a familiar inhabitant: the European eel. But can it account for everything witnesses claim to have seen? With scepticism, humour and a healthy dose of curiosity, Zara and Evelyn dive into the mystery of Morag, and ask whether this elusive monster is real, misunderstood, or best left to legend.

programme.title: Mythland
programme.desc: Evelyn and Zara follow the trail of a local myth to uncover a moving story about industrial decline, community memory and the internet's power to reshape the past.

programme.title: Street Gangs
programme.desc: Best-selling author and ex-gang member Graeme Armstrong travels to forgotten areas of Scotland to shine a light on the allure of gang life. He encounters drill music artists and street gang members, while also exploring his own past. Graeme tries to understand why young people are seduced by the perceived glamour and excitement of gang life by speaking to young people themselves.

programme.title: Street Gangs
programme.desc: Ex gang member and best-selling author Graeme Armstrong explores the underbelly of Dundee as he speaks to ex gang members in local schemes Whitfield and Kirkton and tries to understand the causes of recent civil unrest in the area. In this episode, Graeme focuses on what happens when the perceived glamour wears off and gang life begins to go wrong. Sharing deeply personal stories, Graeme engages with the police and reformed gang members who have nearly lost their lives to this world.

programme.title: Street Gangs
programme.desc: Best-selling author and reformed gang member Graeme Armstrong explores how to escape the gang life. How do ‘young team’ members turn their lives around? Is it even possible? In this episode, Graeme explains that there were only ever three options he could see: death, prison or redemption. This time focusing on Glasgow, Graeme explores the Wyndford Scheme in Maryhill and travels to Glencoe to meet a man who, like himself, managed to turn his life around and leave gangs behind for good.

programme.title: Stevens & McCarthy
programme.desc: Stevens & McCarthy are back with their collection of comic characters, spoofs and musical comedy. At the roll van, Davie is not happy with the chat, a gamer mum loses her cool, and the girls think twinkly lights are the answer to all life's woes.

programme.title: Loop
programme.desc: Ex-Buzzcocks drummer John Maher shares punk memories and his current photography obsession, from his adopted home on the Isle of Harris. We hear how John toured the world supporting the Sex Pistols, and he opens up his scrapbooks to reveal meeting heroes such as Blondie’s Debbie Harry. Having lived a fast-paced life, John moved to Harris 20 years ago, and where he soon picked up his dusty camera and turned his lens to his adopted home. John aims to depict the island in a new way, with the focus not just on the breathtaking landscapes, but also the people and places left behind by humans. We join him as he completes his current project, which features a series of photographs focusing on a local family transforming an old croft into their perfect new home.

programme.desc: Stacey follows three Ukrainian civilians training with British soldiers to fight Russia. In just five weeks, a florist, a welder and a jeweller learn to 'survive and be lethal'.

programme.title: My Mate's a Bad Date
programme.desc: Khalil never remembers his dates’ names, so he calls them all 'baby girl' to skirt around it. Obsessed with looking good, he checks himself out in the reflection of a spoon every 20 minutes on dinner dates and thinks it’s impressive to tell boastful, drunken stories. No wonder the ladies don’t come back for a second date! Cavan is fed up of his best mate Khalil’s dating fails and Khalil not listening to his advice, so he calls on the help of Gen Z's most trusted sex and relationships expert, Oloni, to put this 21-year-old Notts boy on the spot and get him to own up to his bad dating habits. Khalil and Oloni watch video feedback from some very honest friends and exes to show him first hand where it's all going wrong, before Oloni sets Khalil up on a series of first dates that will challenge him to turn him from a bad date to a good date. Under the watchful eye of Oloni and Cavan, can Khalil stop calling his dates 'baby girl', can he resist the urge to check himself out and will he take Oloni's advice on board and stop telling laddish, drunken stories?

programme.title: My Mate's a Bad Date
programme.desc: Larisa is fed up of hearing about her best mate Dami’s latest in a long line of dating fails. He walks out mid-date, interrogates and pulls girls up on their outfits, music choices and lifestyle, and thinks they’re lucky to have him! It’s time for an intervention, so Larisa enlists the help of Gen Z’s most trusted sex and relationships expert Oloni to put the 24-year-old Londoner on the spot and help him own up to his disastrous dating habits. Oloni reviews his dating past and gives him a cold, hard dose of reality as she and Dami watch some honest and sometimes surprising video feedback from family members, friends and even exes to show him where it’s all going wrong. Oloni sets Dami up on a series of first dates that will challenge him to shake off his bad habits and hopefully become a better dater. As Oloni and Larisa watch on, can Dami ditch the interrogation act, stop being so rude to his dates and actually stay to the end?

Tyler insists her ideal date is the male version of herself, but will the male ‘Tyler’ be the perfect match for this feisty female?

programme.title: Beyond Paradise
programme.desc: Humphrey and his team are baffled by a set of reverse burglaries where items are left behind rather than taken. With their only credible suspect being Santa, it’s a race against time to find the real culprit in time for Christmas. The only clues are a pile of ash and glove fibres at each location. With four open cases counting against them, and police HQ breathing down their necks, the team are up against it. They must figure out how the victims are connected, catch the person responsible and save the station in time for the festivities. But when the team make a breakthrough with an unexpected connection to 1973, it’s a bittersweet discovery that makes them reconsider the true meaning of Christmas.

programme.title: Beyond Paradise
programme.desc: Whilst home alone watching family videos, Bob encounters a surprise visitor - his late wife’s ghost, Linda, who has a haunting demand: get out. When there’s a second unsettling encounter and writing on a mirror, Humphrey and the team are called in to investigate. Esther is deeply sceptical, but Humphrey is more than happy to dive into his first haunting. Surely there’s a rational explanation?

programme.title: Mrs Brown's Boys
programme.desc: It may be a time for peace and goodwill, but there is trouble brewing in the Brown household this Christmas. Cathy takes exception to having her mother opening her mail and instigates a clever plan for revenge. Agnes is shocked when the annual Nativity play is cancelled. She vows to stage her own Christmas play. The new priest puts his foot down - but nobody gets in the way of Agnes Brown.

programme.title: Mrs Brown's Boys
programme.desc: Agnes Brown has finally been given permission to stage her own Nativity play and is determined to put on the greatest show on Earth. The only thing standing in her way now is local priest Father Damien, who is insisting that Agnes makes some last-minute changes to her rather unusual script. Will Agnes ever get to play the Virgin Mary?

programme.title: Ghosts
programme.desc: A festive trip down memory lane prompts Pat to question his very identity. The ghosts come up with a surprise Christmas present for Alison, whose family lunch does not go to plan.

programme.title: Ghosts
programme.desc: It’s coming up to Christmas, and Mike’s mum is staying. Betty wants to be helpful, but it isn’t long before she is driving Mike and Alison round the bend. Betty has overstayed her welcome, but Alison and Mike don’t quite have the heart to tell her. Just as she decides to leave of her own volition, Betty suspects something is terribly wrong at Button House. She adopts extreme measures to make the house safe and in doing so endangers the resident Ghosts – will they come out of this unscathed?

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Dependent pest and stay-at-home-daughter Chi is once again forced to contend with life and death, and a long list of things she really ought to have done by now. Her dysfunctional family navigate the fallout of yet another unexpected bereavement, with mixed results. Chi turns to her list of ‘things you should have done’ in this time of need and opts to do ‘get therapy’, something her parents always knew she’d need to do anyway. This sees her path collide with Ruth, a totally unhinged, tough-love grief counsellor, whose questionable methods leave a lot to be desired. Ruth manhandles Chi’s list and vows to help her get over her grief and move on from being able to see her dead parents.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Karen has not only left the family in emotional turmoil but also serious debt. There’s no way Dave can keep up with the mortgage on his single wage, and he faces the very real threat of having to move in with Chi. Out of answers, the family seek advice from grief counsellor Ruth, who advises them to think outside the box and be entrepreneurial. Chi’s not entirely sure what this means, but she needs money. Dave reveals he has a very rich estranged sister, Claudia, whom he hasn’t spoken to since Brexit. It’s risky reaching out to her - she’s a bit of a snob - but if he plays his cards right, he thinks she may well clear his debts.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Grief counsellor Ruth has had enough of Chi feeling down in the dumps due to multiple bereavements in a short space of time, even though it’s a perfectly natural way to feel, and Ruth is literally paid to listen. Ruth sets Chi the task of comparing herself to those less fortunate and instructs her to help out at a food bank - something Ruth does to make herself feel better. Meanwhile, Dave and Lucas are feeling the financial squeeze and settling for a dinner of bread and cress, with only ten pounds left to their name. Chi informs them that she is giving back by going to the food bank and asks if they want to come along.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Chi is rightfully asked if she’s ‘thick’ for bothering an electrician working on an out-of-order lift. For once in her life, Chi is forced to reconcile with her own intelligence. At her weekly grief counselling sessions, Ruth doesn’t exactly hold back, telling Chi she is indeed simple and not to bother seeking adult education. Chi sets out to prove her wrong and breaks into Ramsgate College in search of an education.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Chi’s ghost parents tell her she should really be worried about dying alone and encourage her to find a life partner. Chi casts a very wide and desperate net for potential love interests, approaching almost everyone in Ramsgate with her phone number. Meanwhile, Lucas gets a job at the cinema but is crumbling under the pressure and the perfectly normal expectations of his manager, Kenneth. Lucas resorts to stress-eating the pick ’n’ mix when nobody is looking.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: It’s Chi’s last free therapy session, and Ruth wants to know whether Chi can still see her dead parents or whether she’s learned anything at all from the counselling. But she very much can still see her dead parents; in fact, they were just in the hallway, wearing outdoor clothes and discussing what will become of them if they leave the house. Will they pass on to another plane? Will this be the end of them?

programme.title: My Insta Scammer Friend
programme.desc: In this era of social media, we are given more access to the private lives of celebrities and influencers than ever before. But how well do we really know our favourite online friends? This film explores the murky and, at its worst, toxic, relationship between one influencer and her followers. The infamous viral scandals of pioneering internet sensation Caroline Calloway have captivated audiences across the globe, with some of her followers left feeling duped and scammed. But why did Caroline's actions garner so much attention? And what do influencers owe their followers who built the very foundations of their success?

programme.title: Man Like Mobeen

programme.title: Man Like Mobeen

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France
programme.desc: Sitting between Germany and France, Alsace is frontier land with a cuisine to match. In Strasbourg, Eva stops off at Brasserie Le Tigre for a beer (brassier means ‘to brew’) and a deliciously creamy tarte flambee. Then there's a trip to guide Coralie Andt’s restaurant, known as a winstub, where French wines can be enjoyed with plenty of cheese and sausage – as well as more sausage with sauerkraut cooked in white Riesling wine. With French tarts in a brasserie that serves German-style beer, and German sausage in a winstub serving French white wine, Alsace is defined by its competing national influences.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Wooden shoe lasts are a common sight at antiques fairs, but do you know how they’re made? Natasha Raskin Sharp visits the workshop of cordwainer Payson Muller, originally a stonemason, who turned his talents to making bespoke shoes on hand-carved shoe lasts. He creates them from beech boughs before refining their shape using a knife and rasp. Hoping to cut a few deals of their own are two teams of bargain hunters, shopping for collectibles at Wetherby Racecourse. In blue are couple Martin and Nasreen, and their opponents are married duo Lisamarie and Jamie. Nasreen’s keen eye spots an ornate Russian caviar bowl and spoon, but the price tag is an eye-watering £600. Elsewhere, Jamie comes across a wacky glass vase that resembles a famous artist’s work, but Philip Serrell thinks it’s no masterpiece. At the sale, both teams hope for big profits, but all they can do is watch as their items go under auctioneer Caroline Hawley’s hammer.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: It’s the end of an era on Gardeners' World as Monty approaches his final programme from Longmeadow, the garden he has shared with the nation for the last 16 years. With Ned by his side, he celebrates the enduring pleasures of gardening and serves up one last bulb lasagne. Autumn is a busy time with vegetables to sow, perennials to plant and windfall apples to collect. Carol Klein takes a deep dive into the scientific world of plants. This time, it’s all about the magical properties of their shoots. Joe Swift visits close friend and garden designer Ann-Marie Powell to explore her own garden, a place that has become her solace since the death of her husband last year. In North Yorkshire, there’s a remarkable, pioneering woman on a quest to grow thousands of trees from seed. And a couple in East Grinstead share their combined love for the garden they have created together.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Game show in which 24 players compete across the series, scoring points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the Impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode, there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question.

programme.title: The Answer Run
programme.desc: Comedian Jason Manford hosts an exciting, fast-paced quiz show, where three couples face a series of 50/50 questions which hurtle The Answer Run down towards them. Across three rounds, the couples build up their cash pots, but only one pair can face The Final Run and win the chance to take home their cash prize. Who will swipe their way to victory?

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: George Anderson goes back to school, Flower School, to learn how to make a unique, living flower wreath.

programme.title: The Battle of the River Plate
programme.desc: Second World War naval adventure based on the true story of the pursuit of the seemingly unstoppable German battleship Graf Spee. Allied forces chase the vessel all the way to South America, but after several failed attempts to sink the enemy ship, the Allies find themselves hatching a desperate and audacious plan.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team step back in time at the Beamish Open Air Museum near Newcastle. Amongst the items brought to light are a rare rapier sword allegedly smuggled out of Russia in the props box of the Bolshoi Ballet. We meet a keen collector of battlefield finds known as trench art, and the finest music box to appear on the Roadshow is valued.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This episode comes from the place sometimes dubbed 'the last bastion of free speech in the western world' - the historic Oxford Union. Paul Martin is joined by experts Christina Trevanion and Mark Stacey. Together the team pick out a selection of interesting antiques and collectables to be sold at the local auction house. Christina uncovers a famous fake while Mark gets a religious education after discovering a rare Baptist bust. Paul delves into the history of the auction site which is built on top of infamous Greenham Common.

programme.title: House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Dame Laura Kenny, Minah Shannon, Seann Walsh and Ricky Wilson take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, Michael Sheen. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted with the House of Games record player?

programme.title: Strictly - It Takes Two
programme.desc: Ellie Taylor serves up more unmissable action from the world of Strictly as she chats to more couples about their weekend preparations. Also, costume designer Vicky Gill gives an exclusive look at some of her newest creations.

programme.title: Naturewatch
programme.desc: Chris Packham, Kyle Thomas and Megan McCubbin explore why geese fly in a V formation, why leaves change colour in autumn and why birds eat rocks.

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry
programme.desc: Humanity's very survival depends on water. But global reserves are rapidly shrinking with no end in sight thanks to unmitigated climate change, population growth and poor resource management. Over two-thirds of the global population are faced with water stress, while millions have already been displaced by intense water scarcity which is now replacing oil as the most likely cause of global conflict. Hannah Fry learns about the different ways in which technology could help secure humanity’s future water needs. She witnesses the effects of water scarcity in Kenya and learns about how technological solutions are currently being harnessed to reverse this dire situation.

programme.title: The Secret Genius of Modern Life
programme.desc: Fridges have been quietly ‘keeping things cool’ in the kitchen for over 100 years, and yet most of us barely give them a second thought. Hannah hits the production line with appliance giants Bosch to find the lifeblood at the heart of every fridge and gets a lesson in carrot droop. And she takes a long, cool look at the fridge’s history to reveal how a French monk with a flair for chemistry, a 17th century chicken incubator and an explosive invention in Australia created the ultimate chill.

programme.title: Monty Don’s British Gardens
programme.desc: Monty Don explores the most densely populated part of the country, London and the home counties. He visits some of London’s gardens, including a special one on a barge, as well as a beautifully restored garden close to where he grew up in Hampshire and some gardens known for their different and personal styles of planting.

programme.title: Rise of the Rockstar Chef
programme.desc: Marco chases three Michelin stars, Gordon breaks away to build his own name, and Heston rewrites the rules as huge success brings both fame and a new world of pressure.

programme.title: Cunk on Cinema
programme.desc: Philomena Cunk’s groundbreaking history of cinema begins. Cunk meets Hollywood legends and interrogates the writer of Die Hard, as she starts her quest deep, deep into cinema. She witnesses the shockingly poor picture quality of the earliest films and marvels at the beards of their Victorian inventors; she gasps audibly at the invention of sound; and she critiques some of the supposedly finest creations of Hollywood’s Golden Age. Along the way she interviews filmmakers, actors and critics, including several you’ve definitely heard of, and she (and you) finally discovers the true meaning of The Wizard of Oz.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Planning permission is granted to house 1,300 male migrants next to a village of a few hundred people. Is it the end of the road for the campaigners of Piddington who voted for independence from the UK over the plan? Also, could there be new hope for peace between Russia and Ukraine? With Paddy O'Connell.

programme.title: Hell or High Water
programme.desc: Film thriller. A divorced father and his ex-con older brother resort to a desperate scheme in order to save their family's ranch in west Texas.

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry
programme.desc: With the promise of unimaginable computing power, a global race for quantum supremacy is raging. Hannah Fry looks inside the IBM research facility, one of the oldest tech companies in the world, to uncover the future of quantum technology. She explores the unprecedented potential of quantum computing and how precarious this advanced power may be in the wrong hands. Through her exclusive interviews with world-class experts in quantum technologies, Hannah explores the international quantum arms race between the US and China. She breaks down the implications of this 21st-century race and how a quantum future could change the very nature of humanity.

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry

programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals

programme.title: John Simpson - 60 Years at the BBC
programme.desc: John Simpson looks back at his extraordinary 60-year career at the BBC - reporting on the biggest global stories of the era. In a frank, personal and revealing documentary, he reflects on the changing world he has witnessed: the revolution in Iran that seemed destined to fail, his brutal kidnapping in Beirut, the fall of the Berlin Wall, two wars in Iraq, the invasion of Afghanistan and a mind-altering trip up the Amazon. From the Broadcasting House newsroom in 1966 to World Affairs editor, he looks back at memorable encounters with inspiring leaders and cruel dictators - the figures who have shaped history, including Nelson Mandela, Margaret Thatcher, Saddam Hussein, Colonel Gaddafi and Volodymyr Zelensky. The programme also features his insights into the role of the BBC today and the challenges faced in the age of fake news.

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry

In her quest to learn about the current state of animal communication, Professor Hannah Fry travels across the world, meeting Cash the talking dog in California and deciphering elephant rumbles in Nairobi. She looks into the question of whether the emerging ability to communicate with animals is one that should be exploited.

programme.desc: Calum Clunie has been growing for the Fife veg and flower shows since he was 15 years old, and now he has an allotment in Leven that has dedicated to growing the largest leeks and most dazzling dahlias. Throughout a growing season, Calum let us in on his show-growing secrets as he grows giant onions and massive cabbages alongside stunning sweet peas and delightful dahlias. As a fitting end to the growing year, Calum hosts his own homegrown show in his grandparent’s back garden. It's a real family affair, and there is a visit from a special surprise judge.

programme.title: Angels One Five
programme.desc: Second World War drama relating the Battle of Britain through the eyes of the operations room of a Kent fighter station during the summer of 1940. A young, inexperienced pilot has trouble settling into the routine of squadron life, and his adherence to the rule book puts him out of favour with his comrades. Can he win them round?

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team enter Border country as the Roadshow visits Manderston, near Berwick-upon-Tweed. Amongst the items featured are pieces from Queen Victoria's household, a gruesome man trap and Lord Palmer's collection of rare biscuit tins.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Flog It! comes from Rochester Cathedral in Kent. Antiques expert Elizabeth Talbot falls for a book of fairy tales illustrated by Arthur Rackham, and Adam Partridge discovers an elegant chiming Swiss pocket watch. Presenter Paul Martin meets one of the last remaining survivors of the Dunkirk evacuation during the Second World War.

programme.title: House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Dame Laura Kenny, Minah Shannon, Seann Walsh and Ricky Wilson take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, Michael Sheen. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted with the House of Games record player?

programme.title: Strictly - It Takes Two
programme.desc: Ellie Taylor is on hand with more Strictly exclusives as she’s joined by a brand new all-star panel to break down the couple’s next dances.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Victoria Derbyshire.

programme.title: UEFA Nations League
programme.desc: Live coverage from Hampden as Scotland host North Macedonia in the Nations League.

programme.title: Die Hard with a Vengeance
programme.desc: Classic action blockbuster. John McClane (Bruce Willis) and a store owner, Zeus (Samuel L Jackson), must play a bomber's deadly game as they race around New York trying to stop him.

programme.title: Blue Story
programme.desc: A feature adaptation of Rapman's YouTube series about two young south London friends from different boroughs and their deepening relationships with gangs and girls.

programme.title: This City Is Ours
programme.desc: Desperate to recover their losses, the Phelans strike a deal with Ozzie Thompson. At Jamie and Melissa’s engagement party, Michael and Diana attempt to broker peace with the family. Meanwhile, Freddie spirals further out of Michael’s control.

programme.title: A Course Called Ireland
programme.desc: Hollywood legend Bill Murray begins a journey around Ireland, combining golf with a search for his Irish roots. But travelling with Bill rarely goes to plan. In Kinsale, chance encounters turn a simple walk into an adventure, while friend and golf writer Tom Coyne tries to keep things on track. Golf brought Bill to Ireland, but the best moments often happen far from the course.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Whether you were wading through floods or struggling through a heatwave, 2026 was the year when you could hardly miss our extreme weather. Temperatures in the summer topped 30C for 33 days in a row. Months earlier, some parts of the UK saw 40 consecutive days of rain. The BBC's climate editor Justin Rowlatt investigates the impact of climate change on our weather. He speaks to scientists who warn that hotter summers and wetter winters are likely to become more typical, and asks if enough is being done to adapt our towns and cities to the changing climate. As the cost of living continues to bite, are governments under pressure to ditch some green policies or do they remain committed to tackling climate change?

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: Brinicle invites Pancake onto his radio show but is cross when his accidental burps prove a hit. Pancake soon discovers that fame as ‘burping guy’ has its downsides.

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: Dad and Cosima both think they're the best at pranking. Their prank war quickly spirals out of control, until Big Lizard finally reveals Proxima's real pranking champion!

programme.title: The Weasy Family

programme.title: Super Happy Magic Forest
programme.desc: The Gnome Crystal Mine has ground to a halt, leaving the forest with no crystals, no power supply and melting ice lollies! The heroes are tasked with a quest to find out what has happened and to fix it. It turns out that a slimy beast named Smarg has made the mine her home. But with Hoofius’s fear of gunk getting the better of him, evicting the slippery Smarg is not going to be easy.

programme.title: Grizzy and the Lemmings
programme.desc: The Lemmings use magic Chinese lanterns for sound and light shows.

programme.title: Duck and Frog
