programme.title: Winx Club - The Magic Is Back
programme.desc: The dark magic of Vexius has contaminated Alfea with a lethal residue. The Winx, together with Flora's parents, are searching for a cure to save the flora and fauna of the magic kingdom.

programme.title: The Next Step: Cheer
programme.desc: When a legendary coach abruptly leaves a highly successful cheerleading gym, the team are left in disarray, The Next Step’s Kenzie steps in to take over what’s left of the team, desperate to prove she is more than just a dancer, and that she can build this rag-tag group of athletes into a contender for nationals.

programme.title: Newsround
programme.desc: Topical news magazine for children.

programme.title: Blue Peter
programme.desc: Shini and Abby go head-to-head in an epic Children in Need racing challenge, and Tyler West and Hacker make some delicious Pudsey Pizzas.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve seeks out deadly creatures in miniature, including Australia’s most beautiful spider, Oman’s deadly deathstalker scorpion and a bright blue beauty in Indonesia.

programme.title: Around the World in 80 Gardens
programme.desc: Monty Don visits the world's 80 most inspiring gardens, this time in south east Asia. Since the 19th century, western gardeners have loved tropical gardens. Monty visits the archetype - the mysterious Jim Thompson's Garden in Bangkok. He seeks something more authentic in the Royal Palace gardens and the floating gardens of the canals of Bangkok. In Bali, his preconceptions are challenged again. Is the western picture of the exotic garden a construct?

programme.title: Naturewatch
programme.desc: Chris Packham, Kyle Thomas and Megan McCubbin explore why geese fly in a V formation, why leaves change colour in autumn and why birds eat rocks.

programme.title: My Life at Christmas with Anita Rani
programme.desc: In a rare in-depth interview, Sir Rod Stewart and Penny Lancaster welcome Anita Rani into their home to discuss their lives, family, fame and faith, and how Christmases past and present have shaped them. Across an intimate fireside chat, Christmas crafting in a festive greenhouse and a stroll around the stunning grounds of their countryside home, they reflect on Rod’s rise to fame, Penny’s journey from model to special constable and festive traditions, including exchanging gifts with Elton John.

programme.title: Nadiya’s Everyday Baking
programme.desc: Nadiya shows off some sensational breakfasts to kickstart your weekend, including granola and yoghurt cupcakes, a banana and peanut butter bake, and a crazy-but-delicious breakfast pizza.

programme.title: Ice Cold in Alex
programme.desc: During the German offensive in Libya in 1942, Captain Anson, commander of a motor ambulance convoy, finds himself cut off from his unit with only an old ambulance to take him back to Alexandria. His companions are two young nurses and his sergeant, Tom Pugh. As the little party sets off on the long journey, they meet Van der Poel, a South African captain who begs a lift.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin wants to run for the hills because of a tricky legal issue in Devon. Jacqui is in Eastbourne, where work is already under way at an end-of-terrace. And Dion goes to Northampton, where a smelly cellar is hard to cope with!

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin and his team of experts invite members of the public to bring their antiques to be viewed and valued, with an option to sell at auction.

programme.title: UEFA Nations League
programme.desc: Live coverage as Wales take on Norway in Oslo for their penultimate game in the Nations League.

programme.title: UEFA Nations League
programme.desc: Stephen Watson presents full match coverage from Windsor Park as Northern Ireland take on Ukraine in the Nations League. With just two matches remaining, Northern Ireland remain firmly in contention for promotion from League B. However, Ukraine could provide a major test as Michael O’Neill’s side look to bolster their position ahead of a potentially decisive final fixture. Commentary is by Thomas Kane and Stephen Craigan, with expert analysis from Stuart Dallas, Caragh Hamilton and David Healy.

programme.title: 40 Hits of 1975 at the BBC
programme.desc: Take a musical trip back in time with 40 essential hits from the year 1975, plucked from the BBC’s archives. The punk explosion was two years away, and disco was only just starting to surface, but these 12 months were still packed with classic songs that remain staples to this day. Key moments include ABBA in Blackpool on Seaside Special, the Bay City Rollers riding the wave of Rollermania, and debut hits from key artists who were pioneers in their individual genres, including Bob Marley, Supertramp and Kraftwerk.

programme.title: Godland
programme.desc: In the late 19th century, a young Danish priest is sent to Iceland with a mission to set up a parish in a remote part of the country. Faced with an ambivalent reception by less-than-welcoming locals, he finds that his zeal, faith and sense of reality start to drift as he ventures deeper into the Icelandic landscape. In Danish and Icelandic with English subtitles.

programme.title: This City Is Ours
programme.desc: The tragic events of the party send shock waves through the Phelans. As dangerous secrets threaten to come to light, Michael is forced to make a difficult confession to Diana. Meanwhile, unseen dangers close in, and it becomes clear no-one is safe.

programme.title: Celebrity Race Across the World
programme.desc: The second leg of the race takes the teams across the heart of Borneo to a modern metropolis on its eastern coast and their second checkpoint.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: My Life at Christmas with Anita Rani
programme.desc: Anita Rani meets Paralympian and broadcaster Ade Adepitan to hear his inspirational life story and how sport, spirituality and the festive season have shaped him, from contracting polio as a toddler in Nigeria, to growing up with a disability in east London in the 1970s, to the rocky road that led to Paralympic glory with the British wheelchair basketball team. Now a respected broadcaster, Ade shines a light on the causes that are close to his heart.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Figures for the first seven months of the year show milk production in Northern Ireland is heading for a record year. But fluctuating prices, rising costs and the ever-present threat of disease have left many dairy businesses under financial pressure. Alongside local farmer Emily McGowan, Charlotte Smith and Adam Henson explore how dairy farmers across County Antrim, one of Northern Ireland's most productive dairy regions, are turning to tech and innovative business models to build a more resilient future. Adam also introduces this year’s BBC Food and Farming Awards Countryfile Young Countryside Champion nominees.

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: Dougie is in Castlemilk housing estate on the southern edge of Glasgow, where he explores a local nature reserve that has transformed from perceived no-go zone to a thriving, green place. Arlene steps back in time in Aberdeenshire as she visits a rare shoemaker's workshop that shut up shop over 80 years ago. She meets the locals carefully conserving the shop’s contents. Anne is in the Black Isle, finding out about a charity funded by Children in Need that is providing bereavement support across the Highlands. And Dougie watches on as one couple’s herd of Aberdeen Angus cattle leaves the farm for good to go under the hammer at a dispersal sale.

programme.title: BBC Children in Need
programme.desc: Radio 1 presenter Sian Eleri follows Pudsey Bear’s clues on a road trip around Wales to meet the special young people and projects benefiting from BBC Children in Need funding.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Andi Oliver takes a classic British dessert and transforms it into a savoury number with her three cheese and leek bread and butter pudding. She then grills slices of it with a rarebit sauce on top, serving it with a leek and spinach veloute. Niklas Ekstedt brings the taste of Sweden to the studio with the iconic Jansson's temptation, which he serves alongside a deliciously fatty pork chop. Sabrina Ghayour serves up three tasty treats that are perfect for sharing: lamb barberry and pine nut koftas, pomegranate-glazed aubergines, and muhammara dip. Rick Stein has a dish inspired by his travels, while Paul A Young makes maraschino cherry and almond truffles. And Mel C is in the hot seat to face either her food heaven, roast lamb, or her food hell, okra. Meanwhile, Rick Stein has a peek behind the scenes at how the filming of his shows doesn’t always go to plan, and Clive Myrie gets a taste of Caribbean honey.

programme.title: Best Bakes Ever
programme.desc: With Britain more obsessed with baking than ever, actress and cake expert Jane Asher brings together a selection of recipes from the nation's favourite television chefs, for 'The Best Bakes Ever'. Each episode gives baking fans another chance to experience classic dishes from the likes of the James Martin, Mary Berry and Paul Hollywood, the Hairy Bikers, Raymond Blanc, Nigella Lawson, Tom Kerridge, Lorraine Pascale and Rachel Khoo. There's added insight and appreciation from Jane herself too. Whether its cakes, pies, puddings or main courses - this greatest hits of baking is a must for anyone with a need to knead, and should help inspire even more of us to start getting creative in the kitchen.

programme.title: Nigel Slater's Simple Suppers
programme.desc: Nigel Slater creates simple but delicious meals from ingredients that are often overlooked, including a lentil and chard stew.

programme.title: Jane Eyre
programme.desc: Charlotte Bronte's classic about an orphan girl who grows up to become a governess in a gloomy manor in Yorkshire, where she falls in love with the mysterious Edward Rochester.

programme.title: Spellbound
programme.desc: Gripping Hitchcock thriller in which a psychoanalyst falls in love with her new boss, knowing that he is an amnesiac who may be a killer and an impostor. Characteristically Hitchcockian twists blur reality and imagination as the psychoanalyst struggles to restore his memory. A dream sequence designed by Salvador Dali adds to the suspense.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This episode contains a collection of interesting and previously unseen finds from the show's travels round the country, visiting Margam Country Park in south Wales, Highcliffe Castle in Dorset and Powderham Castle in Devon. The experts include Catherine Southon, Adam Partridge, Philip Serrell, Will Axon, Christina Trevanion and Mark Stacey, with items ranging from a South African Krugerrand coin to a rare walnut-shaped Japanese flintlock. Paul also takes a look at the treasures and lavish interiors at Firle Place in east Sussex.

programme.title: Golf: Tour Championship
programme.desc: Final day highlights as the DP World Tour season reaches its climax. The winner of the Race to Dubai is crowned, with Northern Ireland’s Rory McIlroy having won the last four editions. McIlroy has won seven Race to Dubai titles, putting him one behind Colin Montgomerie’s all-time record. Spain’s Engenio Chacarra has enjoyed an incredible breakout season, and the USA’s Patrick Reed is firmly in the mix with two wins to his name. Open champion Ryan Fox and PGA champion Aaron Rai also tee it up on the Earth Course at Jumeirah Golf Estates in Dubai. The top ten DP World Tour members not already exempt will earn a PGA Tour card for the 2027 season.

programme.title: Celebrity Race Across the World
programme.desc: The third leg of the race sees the teams leave behind the ancient jungles of Borneo to reach the island of Sulawesi, an Indonesian wonderland that lies far from the tourist trail. But with the end of Ramadan fast approaching, the teams must negotiate the crowds heading home for Eid al-Fitr.

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: As the days grow longer, the MacDonalds round up their pregnant Highland cattle on the tiny island of Vallay off North Uist for a prenatal check up and vitamin boost. In Newtonmore in the Cairngorms, Jenni’s new alpaca arena is finally finished, which means her menagerie of alpacas, donkeys and goats must be moved to their new home. Nikki and Ollie are speculating to accumulate in Moray, splashing out on a new honesty shack.

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France
programme.desc: Paris is home to more award-winning pastry chefs than anywhere else in the world. Here, the day revolves around patisserie. Morning begins with the buttery flakes of a croissant. At midday, a baguette tucked under the arm signals lunch. And by the afternoon, mouthwatering sweet treats are savoured like miniature works of art. Resistance is futile, and Eva is seduced by the Paris-Brest, a rum baba, the macaron, a mango cake and dahlia, to name just a few.

programme.title: Ireland with Simon Reeve
programme.desc: Simon begins his journey in the south of Ireland, paramotoring with an Irish explorer. On the west coast, he does a spot of surfing before climbing Croagh Patrick in honour of Ireland's patron saint. This leg of his journey ends in Malin Head, Ireland's most northerly point.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Bob and Paul are in County Durham, fishing the River Tees for a rare species of wild brown trout. They navigate the area through the lens of a six-year-old Bob as he takes Paul on a trip along the landscapes of his youth. Bob lost his dad when he was very young, but some of the memories he holds dear to him are of the fishing trips they used to go on. Later, Bob invites their old friend Reece Shearsmith to dinner, who has some particularly spooky local tales to tell them about the River Tees.

programme.title: A Course Called Ireland
programme.desc: As Bill's 75th birthday approaches, brother Joel joins the adventure, bringing some Murray family rivalry to the golf course. Comedian Joanne McNally attempts her first ever round, while a bouncing boat trip to the Cliffs of Moher brings further unexpected encounters. Then friends and familiar faces gather to celebrate a milestone birthday – and a reflective Bill looks ahead to what might come next.

programme.title: Later... with Jools Holland
programme.desc: Jools Holland introduces a special edition of the show starring one of the biggest bands in the world, Fontaines D.C. Marking the release of their album Dopamine Chamber, the Dublin five-piece take to the stage for an intimate performance filmed at Alexandra Palace Theatre in north London. Ahead of a huge global arena and stadium tour, including two nights at the iconic Slane Castle in Ireland, the band play exclusive first performances of tracks alongside unique versions of favourites from their extensive songbook.

programme.title: The Hurt Locker
programme.desc: Baghdad, 2004. A maverick member of a US military unit tackling IEDs and bomb disposal aggravates his teammates. Powerful Oscar- and BAFTA-winning drama.

programme.title: Duck and Frog
programme.desc: Duck and Frog are working at a supermarket alongside Toad and Flamingo, who keep ruining Duck and Frog's hard work to make them look bad. Why are they being so mean?

programme.desc: Duck is working in a florist's, and Frog is a customer who wants to send flowers to his secret crush. However, his strong fragrance sends Duck into a destructive sneezing frenzy.

programme.desc: Steve Backshall meets the most sinister shark in our seas. The ragged tooth shark has a mouth that's overflowing with terrifying teeth. But why does it need such gnarly gnashers? Steve heads out on a dive after dark to see these fearsome fangs for himself, before revealing their sinister secret in his shark lab.

programme.desc: The boys test their horsepower to the max on Stone Age Top Gear, Charles Dickens sings about his life and books, the Greek philosophers host weird dinner parties on Historical Come Dine with Me, and Vlad the Impaler reveals his horrible new plan for keeping out the neighbours.

programme.desc: Steve and the team are on the search for deadly animals in the steaming swamps of the southern USA. The contenders are everywhere, not least the alligators that live in just about every pond and lake. But the first animal on the list is a complete surprise, a monster fish with two rows of sharp fangs that certainly keeps Steve on his toes. The crew find themselves up to their armpits in a swamp hoping to find a deadly snake with the unusual name of cottonmouth. Last but not least, Steve and his team come face to face with an enormous record-breaking predatory turtle.

programme.title: Operation Ouch!
programme.desc: The doctors reveal how important cartilage is to your body with the help of a suit of armour, and they find out what it takes to be a hospital porter in Operation Takeover. Dr Chris meets Nala the dog to see how she helps patients in hospital, and we meet two more of our ouch patients to find out what it's like to be a regular hospital patient. Meanwhile, in accident and emergency, one patient arrives by air ambulance and another is treated for a spring stuck in his thumb.

programme.title: Cooking Buddies
programme.desc: Buddy and Conker are joined by Taye, a young street artist who wants to make a surprise birthday meal for his dad, who loves crispy chicken. Together, they make the crispiest, most delicious fried chicken, served up with homemade slaw, potato wedges and corn on the cob in what must be the best birthday present ever! In return for Buddy’s help, Taye shares some of his artistic skills and shows him how to create his very own bubble-writing signature. Join Buddy, Conker and Taye as they create a work of art both on paper and on a plate with a great homemade takeaway! You can get all of Buddy’s recipes, and loads more, at bbc.co.uk/food

programme.title: Blow Your Mind
programme.desc: Dr Chris and Dr Xand van Tulleken bring you the top experts on the planet to show you things that will blow your mind. In this episode they find out the differences between dogs and wolves. Chris Packham visits some perfume-loving wolves, watches some tiny wolf cubs and discovers how dogs and wolves react in the same experiment.

programme.desc: Doctor Who fan Adam wants a den where he can celebrate his favourite TV show and pursue his passion for drama. His den story takes him on an incredible voyage of discovery that includes a surprise chat with someone very special.

But the ship seems to be haunted by ghostly voices, which a quick dip below the water line reveals to be hundreds of barnacles stuck to the ship. As the ship drifts into waters too cold for the barnacles, the Octonauts must find a way to tow it to warmer waters before it sinks or falls apart.

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: Volcanic smoke blocks the three Proximan suns, which causes Big Lizard to become worryingly cold. Cosima's on the case and comes up with a superhot solution!

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: Brinicle invites his Piri friends round to taste his brilliant brioche. Yuk - it’s chewy and hasn't risen at all! Despite this, Brinicle announces he has entered a baking competition. A disaster looms, but Flutter has an idea.

programme.title: Do Not Watch This Show
programme.desc: A spooky ghost is dropping by, and Wizz tries to protect everyone from the fright.

programme.title: Duck and Frog
programme.desc: Frog is walking in the rain when he spots Duck's beach-themed window display and decides it's the perfect place to relax in the sun for a while.

programme.title: Boy Girl Dog Cat Mouse Cheese
programme.desc: Since she doesn't have a birthday, Cheese demands a big party every year. However, this year her siblings couldn’t be bothered to organise it and it's a complete flop. How can the kids make it up to Cheese?

programme.title: The Next Step: Cheer
programme.desc: When a legendary coach abruptly leaves a highly successful cheerleading gym, the team are left in disarray, The Next Step’s Kenzie steps in to take over what’s left of the team, desperate to prove she is more than just a dancer, and that she can build this rag-tag group of athletes into a contender for nationals.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: A helicopter trip over the vast expanse of Brazil's northern savannah helps adventurer Steve Backshall find his next contender for the Deadly 60. He is in search of the elusive giant anteater, but can he get close enough to film one for his list? A chance encounter with a tough little owl with an ingenious way of catching its supper captures Steve's attention and the rainforest lives up to its name as a very wet team ventures out at night looking for some of the world's deadliest bugs.

programme.title: Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: When two different pieces of flat-pack furniture are delivered to the Farmer and Bitzer, confusion ensues as they start to mix up the pieces. Shaun and the flock are forced to give them a lesson in following instructions.

programme.title: Dennis & Gnasher Unleashed!
programme.desc: JJ applies for an elite sporting school. However, not realising it's miles away from Beanotown, he needs to do badly in the sporting assessment to get out of it.

programme.title: Danger Mouse
programme.desc: Calling all agents! Join Danger Mouse on his hilarious, high-stakes missions as he tries to defeat evil - saving London, the world and, most importantly, his sidekick, Penfold.

programme.title: Super Happy Magic Forest
programme.desc: Twinkle uses her excellent pocket beast card skills when on a quest to rescue the missing Council of Happiness from Grackle the Giant.

When Lola and her imaginary friend Soren Lorenson find they have to transport an elephant back to the jungle, Soren persuades Lola that using the rocket is a really good idea.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: It's a stormy day outside. The Squirrels are busy playing and Duggee is making banana muffins. A big dark cloud hovers over the clubhouse, it wobbles and we hear a massive BOOM! Fortunately, Duggee has his brave banana badge, so he knows exactly how to help them overcome their fears.

Duggee and the Squirrels go off and investigate, following the sneezes all the way to a polar bear with a very bad cold. He needs a hanky. What could they use instead?

They don't all like it at first, so let’s hope they change their minds when they taste the finished dish. Marian works hard layering peppers, tomatoes and feta in beautiful Bulgarian pots. He then puts an egg on top of each one before it cooks in the oven. When his friends arrive, Marian is wearing traditional national dress and gives them all a traditional bracelet as a gift.

programme.title: I Can Grow It

The first idea is a hilarious hairdo pot, the Mini Monsters make a variety of cheese box octopuses, and the Magic Monster Mirror brings a call from Rebecca’s aunt. Finally, the Recycling Express arrives with some buttons that Murphi and Rebecca use to create a brilliant box robot.

Duggee starts to sing a song and marches ahead, while the Squirrels march behind him and join in. Hold on, what's that noise? It's Mrs Weaver the beaver, and she's struggling to get her cubs to sleep with all that noise!

programme.title: Octonauts

programme.title: Vida the Vet

Every year, salmon swim from the oceans where they live all the way upstream to calm, shallow rivers to lay their eggs. On the way they have to leap up waterfalls, jump fish ladders and dash past hungry bears who try to catch them. Kyan thinks these fish are even better at fantastic gymnastics than he is! Ubercorn sets those co-ordinates for the Kenai River, Alaska and the Go Jetters make their way to see the salmon run for themselves.

programme.title: Zog

programme.title: Bluey

programme.title: Tralala
programme.desc: Pasilio loves to keep lost things, but Tralala knows they need to go back to their owners.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi wants her dads to stop doing chores and to dance with her. She wishes to be the oldest so that she can set the rules. Suddenly, Jake and Dash turn into babies, leaving Rafi in charge! It’s funny at first, but soon the mess grows. Rafi realises being a grown-up means taking responsibility. She cleverly mixes tidying with dancing, showing them chores can be fun too. When the wish ends, her dads return to normal and are proud of Rafi’s maturity and teamwork.

programme.desc: After doing some exercise to start the day, Nick and Norman spot a moth and a sloth and realise that sometimes it's fun to take things nice and slow.

When Elder Kitten reminds him that he is DJing at the Befriend a Bug party later, he starts practising his beatboxing. He notices some caterpillars on a nearby branch dancing to the music, but when he tries to approach them, they get frightened and curl up. Realising that they aren't afraid of him while he makes music, Love Monster builds them a miniature stage and happily performs for them. But when the party starts, they all appear to have vanished - or so it seems...

His sense of fun and adventure has faded, and he finds it hard to enjoy the things he once loved. That is, until he meets Pudsey Bear. Together, they embark on a magical journey as Pudsey takes Jai to meet some inspiring children who help him to confront his struggles through their shared experience. Because of the support that each of them gives to Jai, he realises that, even in a world that feels overwhelming, hope and joy still exist.
